claims.text: Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment are vulnerable to attack by molten aluminum.
Applying a thin chromium surface coating will improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
The chromium coating reacts with molten aluminum at the interface.
The interfacial reaction forms a stable Cr-Al intermetallic phase.
The Cr-Al intermetallic phase acts as a diffusion barrier.
The proposed diffusion barrier slows aluminum ingress into the boride substrate.
Formation of a passivating intermetallic surface layer reduces the rate of corrosive attack by molten aluminum.
The chromium coating will decrease weight loss relative to an uncoated boride component under identical exposure conditions.
The chromium coating will decrease aluminum penetration depth relative to an uncoated boride component under identical exposure conditions.
Chromium-coated specimens will show at least approximately a 30% improvement in corrosion indicators relative to uncoated controls.
The corrosion-resistance benefit will persist at typical hot-dip aluminum-plating temperatures and immersion times.
Defects that compromise coating quality may diminish the corrosion-resistance benefit.
Extreme thermal cycling beyond standard operating conditions may diminish the corrosion-resistance benefit.
Approximately 660 degrees Celsius is representative of operational molten-aluminum exposure in the proposed application.
